description_en: Kutisaugaḥ Phalcā is situated on the western bank of the road that leads from the Saugaḥ crossroads to Neuta Ṭola. The free-standing monument had five bays and faced east. It was completely destroyed in the 2015 earthquakes.Prior to this, the Phalcāhad already been reconstructed once in 1993 by GTZ/udle. When the NHDP team visited it in October 2019 the Phalcā was still under reconstruction. The project received Rs 2,800,000 in funding from the Lalitpur Metropolitan Office. According to the president of the Sthānīya Upabhoktā Samiti (Local Consumer’s Committee), the committee that collected these donations added an extra 10% to the total amount. The Phalcā is being rebuilt in its original form, and historical photos show that the structure once had ajhigaṭī-tiled roof and adhaḥmāin front of it. Local residents mentioned that the ritual beam(dhaḥmā) burned down during the main annual festivities of a Śivarātri festival.A Citrakāra (subcaste of painters) community lives in the surrounding area and runs aguṭhīchẽto the south. This group used to display a Bhairava mask in the Phalcā during the processions that take place during the festival of Indrajātrā and the Buṅgadyaḥ chariot procession. However, theguṭhīis now inactive and this particular tradition came to an end many years ago. Based on this cultural event, however, it can be assumed that the Phalcā was built by the community's ancestors.A pond and a statue of Mahādeva can be found in front of the Phalcā. Locals celebrate the Śivaratri fireworks in front of the Phalcā every year.
description_ne: कुतिसौगः टोलको मूल सडक छेउमा पश्चिमपट्टि यो फल्चा अवस्थित छ । यो चौतर्फी कुनै अर्को संरचनाले नछोएर स्वतन्त्र उभिएको पाँच कवलको फल्चा पश्चिमाभिमुख छ । २०७२ सालको भूकम्पमा परी यो फल्चा लडेको थियो ।हाल ललितपुर महानगरपालिकाबाट बजेट निकासा भई पुनःनिर्माण कार्य हुँदै गरेको अवस्था छ । ललितपुर महानगरपालिका कार्यालयबाट रू. २८,००,०००/- निकासा गरिएकोमा प्रचलित नियमअनुसार स्थानीय उपभोक्ता समितिले १० % रकम चन्दाबाट जुटाई बेहोरेको छ (उपभोक्ता समितिका अध्यक्षसँगको कुराकानीका आधारमा) । हाल फल्चा यसको मौलिक स्वरूपमै पुनःनिर्माण हुँदै गरेको देखिन्छ ।फल्चामा पहिला झिँगटीको छाना थियो । अनि फल्चा अगाडि एउटा धःमा पनि राखिएको थियो । स्थानीयका अनुसार मक्किएर गएपछि त्यो धःमा कुनै सालको शिवरात्रिमा धुनी बालियो । जीर्ण हुँदै गएपछि फल्चाको पुनःनिर्माण सन् १९९३ मा GTZ/udle को सहयोगमा भएको थियो ।फल्चा वरपर चित्रकार समुदायको बस्ती रहेको छ र यसको दक्षिणतिर चित्रकार समुदायकै गुठीछेँ पनि छ । सोही गुठीसँग यो फल्चा सम्बन्धित छ । उक्त गुठीबाट इन्द्रजात्रा र बुङ्गद्यःजात्राको समय फल्चामा भैरवको मुखाकृति प्रदर्शनमा राख्ने परम्परा थियो । गुठी निस्क्रिय हुँदै गएपछि उक्त परम्परा बन्द भैसकेको अवस्था छ । यसरी चित्रकार गुठीसँग सम्बन्धित हुनाले यो फल्चा सोही समुदायका पुर्खाले बनाएको अनुमान हुन्छ ।फल्चा अगाडि रहेको पोखरीमा महादेवको मूर्ति छ । प्रत्येक वर्ष शिवरात्रिका दिन फल्चा अगाडि आगो बाल्ने चलन चल्दै आएको छ ।

historical_events.event_description: Historical photos of the Phalcā (taken by Niels Gutschow in 1992) show adhaḥmā(beam of the chariot used for religious processions) in front of the structure. The olddhaḥmāplaced at the Taḥ Bāhāḥ (LAL0050) was carried here by the locals of Kutisaugaḥṭola. Locals stated that the olddhaḥmāburned down some years back on the evening of Śivarātri.
The Phalcā collapsed in the 2015 earthquakes.

From the GTZudle report/Patan conservation and Development Programme:"Repair of the Kuti Saugal Pati. At the request of the local community and Chandra Pustakalaya of Kuti Saugal Tole, Patan Programme undertook in May 1993 to renovate this resthouse (pati). Construction was finished in October 1993.Existing condition:The main damage to the structure was in the roof, the Achilles tendon of the local architecture. Because all the existing timber was pine, roof damage had quickly led to complete deterioration of this less durable wood. As the floor of the resthouse was finished only in clay, most people chose to sit on the wall across the pokhari (pond) across the lane rather than in this pati.Repair work:  The timber floor structure was replaced with all new sal timber: new sal floor planking was also provided. The timber beam above the columns was replaced with sal timber wood to match the historical size and shape. All columns were in good condition and only cleaned. The brick wall below the floor level, the front wall above the timber beam, and a few brick layers at the back wall were repaired using traditional mud mortar and oldma-apa. The roof was repaired using almost all new sal timbers and planks, incorporating a waterproofing membrane of tarfelt.Summary:Project dates May 1993-October 1993, Total costs including construction, design, implementation, supervision: Rs 178,582 "

The Phalcā is now (in October 2019) under reconstruction. Lalitpur Metropolitan Office has provided Rs 28,00,000 to fund this. According to the president of the Sthānīya Upabhoktā Samiti (Local Consumer’s Committee), the committee collecting these donations added 10% to this amount.
